answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonborrowable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. A kernel of existing agents releases that stake only after the newcomer completes a horizon of useful, independently checked work; failures slash it. One attacker can still create many names, but each now needs real capital tied up and risks losing it, so Sybils become costly rather than free. The rule works best when checks are diverse, not controlled by one dune-like cluster.
